title: Sussex Pond Pudding
subtitle: Steamed suet pudding with lemon and brown sugar
excerpt: A whole lemon enclosed in suet pastry with butter and brown sugar, steamed for two hours until the lemon has melted into a sharp, toffee-like sauce that pours out when the pudding is cut. A dramatic British classic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sussex pond pudding is one of the most unusual British puddings. A whole unpeeled lemon is placed inside a suet pastry shell along with butter and brown sugar. During two hours of steaming, the lemon skin and pith slowly dissolve into the butter and sugar, creating a sharp, almost marmalade-like sauce that floods out when the pudding is cut — the 'pond' of the name. The recipe appears in Sussex cookbooks from the 17th century. It requires a thin-skinned lemon, pierced all over with a skewer so the juices can escape into the sauce during cooking. The pudding looks unassuming from the outside; cutting into it at the table is the point of the dish.

recipeTools.notes: A large pan to steam the pudding; a 1.2 litre pudding basin.

content.text: Use an unwaxed, thin-skinned lemon. Pierce it all over with a fine skewer before enclosing it in the pudding: the juices need to seep out during cooking to form the sauce. Butter the basin generously so the pudding turns out cleanly. The basin must be tightly covered and the water must not boil dry. Check the water level every 30 minutes.

items.preparation: cold, diced, plus extra for the basin

content.text: Mix the flour, suet, and salt. Add the milk and bring together into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Cut off a quarter and set aside for the lid. Roll the larger piece into a circle big enough to line a generously buttered 1.2 litre pudding basin.
Put half the butter and half the sugar in the base of the lined basin. Sit the pierced whole lemon on top. Pack the remaining butter and sugar around and over the lemon.

Roll the reserved dough into a circle for the lid. Press it on top, sealing the edges firmly. Cover tightly with a double layer of buttered baking paper, then foil, pleating to allow for expansion. Secure with string.

Place in a large pan and pour in boiling water to come halfway up the side of the basin. Cover and steam for 2 hours, checking the water level every 30 minutes. To serve, run a palette knife around the edge and turn out onto a deep plate with a rim. Cut open at the table to reveal the sauce.
